newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba will hold local elections in October.
newsitem.headline: Cuba will hold local elections in October.

text.p: Cuba will hold local government elections on Oct. 19 to choose delegates to its 169 municipal assemblies, the ruling Council of State said on Saturday.
The announcement came during a ceremony marking the birthdays of two heroes of Cuban history, 19th-century independence fighter Antonio Maceo and Argentine-born guerrilla icon Ernesto "Che" Guevara.

The Municipal Assemblies of People's Power, whose members will be chosen in October, form the lowest tier of Cuba's single-party system of government, in which only the ruling Communist Party is legally recognised.
The assemblies deal with local issues and implement national policies at the grass roots. Elections for delegates are held every two-and-a-half years.
Under Cuban law, voters choose from a minimum of two candidates. Voting is not obligatory but is presented by the authorities as a patriotic duty.
The Council of State said a second round of voting would be held on Oct. 26 to decide the winner in areas where no candidate had more than 50 percent of the total vote.
Cuban leaders, rejecting foreign criticism of the island's political system, have vowed to maintain one-party socialism.
